note: Our own encodings. Two rules, written in all three shapes, so the only thing that changes between the columns is the modelling.

target.title: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS
target.why: One target, so the only thing that changes between the three columns is the modelling. Ubuntu because both rules are published for it, by DISA, and a reader can check them.

rules.label: Rule 1, data at rest
rules.statement: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS handling data requiring data-at-rest protections must employ cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure and modification of the information at rest.
rules.why_chosen: A binary condition with no value to set. It is the simple case, and it is the one all three approaches already have an analogue for.

rules.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
rules.statement: Ubuntu 24.04 LTS must enforce a minimum 15-character password length.
rules.why_chosen: The same shape as the first rule but carrying a value, so it is the rule that shows where each approach puts a parameter. Publishers disagree on the number, which is why the number has to live somewhere addressable.

catalog-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
catalog-first.shows: A control. The requirement is the control's statement, the check is named in an assessment-method part, and a value, where there is one, is a control parameter.

catalog-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
catalog-first.shows: A control. The requirement is the control's statement, the check is named in an assessment-method part, and a value, where there is one, is a control parameter.

component-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
component-first.shows: A rules entry on the component the rule applies to. The rule is first-class rather than a prop, and a value is a rule param set by the control implementation.

component-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
component-first.shows: A rules entry on the component the rule applies to. The rule is first-class rather than a prop, and a value is a rule param set by the control implementation.

assessment-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
assessment-first.shows: An activity. The requirement is the activity title, the work is in its steps, and the identifiers stay in the publisher's own namespace.

assessment-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
assessment-first.shows: An activity. The requirement is the activity title, the work is in its steps, and the identifiers stay in the publisher's own namespace.

catalog-first.label: Both rules and their control ties
catalog-first.shows: A whole document of its own. Metadata and a four-field provenance block come before the first map, and both ends of a map must be a control or a statement.

component-first.label: Both rules and their control ties
component-first.shows: No second document, and two ties in one place. The implemented requirement ties the component to the control, which OSCAL already does; implementing-rules ties the rule to it, which it does not.

assessment-first.label: Both rules and their control ties
assessment-first.shows: Named on the activity itself. No second document and no second identifier, so nothing can fall out of step, and nothing else can reuse the tie.

catalog-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
catalog-first.shows: The check is a software component whose title is the identifier the control's assessment-method part named.

catalog-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
catalog-first.shows: The check is a software component whose title is the identifier the control's assessment-method part named.

component-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
component-first.shows: Two components, not one. The rule sits on the product; the check sits on a second component of type validation, one per engine, and reaches back by rule id and the uuid of the component the rule belongs to.

component-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
component-first.shows: Two components, not one. The rule sits on the product; the check sits on a second component of type validation, one per engine, and reaches back by rule id and the uuid of the component the rule belongs to.

assessment-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
assessment-first.shows: The steps are the check, and a check prop names it. Put that prop on the step and the plan can ask for one item; put it on the activity and one invocation covers every step beneath. The runner decides which.

assessment-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
assessment-first.shows: The steps are the check, and a check prop names it. Put that prop on the step and the plan can ask for one item; put it on the activity and one invocation covers every step beneath. The runner decides which.

assessment-first.label: Multiple tests, with the check at the activity level
assessment-first.shows: The same two checks named on the activity instead, for a runner that executes in bulk. One invocation, every step beneath it.

catalog-first.label: What the checks run against
catalog-first.shows: Every component the catalog applies to, taken together.

component-first.label: What the checks run against
component-first.shows: The components carrying the rules, named by uuid.

component-first.label: The same component, copied into the assessor's plan
component-first.shows: The component definition carried into an assessment plan as an asset. The checks travel with the component that runs them, and each names the component it tests.

assessment-first.label: What the checks run against
assessment-first.shows: One host, named explicitly as an inventory item.

catalog-first.label: What the run reads: the check components
catalog-first.shows: The check components the run is handed. What runs them is never named.

catalog-first.label: What the run produces: the response in the plan of record
catalog-first.shows: A by-component saying the control is met. Nothing on it names the check that produced it.

component-first.label: What the run reads: the checks it is handed
component-first.shows: The checks the run is handed, each naming its rule and its subject.

component-first.label: What the run produces: the assertion in the plan of record
component-first.shows: The response the run writes, carrying implementing-rules so the assertion and its check travel together.

component-first.label: What the run reads: the same checks, in the assessor's plan
component-first.shows: The same definition, taken into a plan the assessor owns. The checks travel with it.

component-first.label: What the run produces: the observation
component-first.shows: The check identifier joins back to what ran, and the subject is a host rather than a component.

assessment-first.label: What the run reads: the checks and the platform
assessment-first.shows: The checks and what runs them, in one plan the assessor owns.

assessment-first.label: What the run produces: the observation
assessment-first.shows: The observation names the activity that ran. No plan of record has to exist for it to resolve.

catalog-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
catalog-first.shows: A by-component response in the SSP, against the product control.

catalog-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
catalog-first.shows: A by-component response in the SSP, against the product control.

component-first.label: Rule 1, data at rest
component-first.shows: The same shape, against the framework control, and carrying implementing-rules so the claim names the rule it rests on.

component-first.label: Rule 2, minimum password length
component-first.shows: The same shape, against the framework control, and carrying implementing-rules so the claim names the rule it rests on.

assessment-first.label: One pointer, covering both rules
assessment-first.shows: Not the claim, but where it lives. import-ssp resolves to a back-matter resource naming the system security plan, and a second resource covers the case where no OSCAL one exists.

catalog-first.shows: A finding, targeting the product control's statement.

catalog-first.shows: A finding, targeting the product control's statement.

component-first.shows: An observation carrying the check id and its result.
